name: Master File Navigation
description: Learn essential file and folder operations that every computer user should know

character.welcomeMessage:
আছস? Ready to become a file management pro? 📁
I'll teach you everything about files and folders!
It's easier than you think!
character.completionMessage:
🎉 Amazing! You've mastered the basics of file navigation!
Now you can organize your computer like a pro!
আছস? that wasn't hard at all, right? 😊

steps.detailedInstruction: On Windows: Click the folder icon in your taskbar or press Windows key + E. On Mac: Click the Finder icon in your dock or press Cmd + Space and type 'Finder'.
steps.successMessage: Perfect! File Explorer is open. Now let's navigate to your Desktop.

errorMessages.timeout: Take your time! Look for a folder icon to open File Explorer.
errorMessages.wrongApp: Make sure you open File Explorer or Finder, not a web browser.

hints: Windows: Look for a yellow folder icon in your taskbar
Windows: You can also press Windows key + E
Mac: Look for the Finder icon (blue and white face) in your dock
The window should show your folders and files

steps.detailedInstruction: In File Explorer/Finder, click on 'Desktop' in the left sidebar, or navigate to Desktop through your user folder. You should see the same files and folders that are on your desktop screen.
steps.successMessage: Great! You're now in the Desktop folder. Let's create a new folder here.

errorMessages.timeout: Look for 'Desktop' in the left sidebar and click on it.
errorMessages.wrongLocation: Make sure you're in the Desktop folder, not another location.

hints: Look for 'Desktop' in the left sidebar and click it
The address bar should show 'Desktop' or your username/Desktop
You should see the same items as on your desktop screen
If you can't find it, try clicking on your username first

steps.instruction: Right-click in empty space and create a new folder
steps.detailedInstruction: Right-click in an empty area of the Desktop folder (not on any existing file). Select 'New' > 'Folder' from the menu. A new folder will appear ready to be named.
steps.successMessage: Excellent! You created a new folder. Now let's give it a meaningful name.

errorMessages.timeout: Right-click in an empty space (not on a file) and select New > Folder.
errorMessages.noFolder: Make sure you select 'New' > 'Folder' from the right-click menu.

hints: Right-click in an empty area, not on an existing file
Look for 'New' in the menu, then 'Folder'
A new folder should appear with a highlighted name
Different systems might say 'New Folder' or 'Create Folder'

steps.instruction: Name the folder 'LearningWithAsos' and press Enter
steps.detailedInstruction: The new folder should have its name highlighted. Type 'LearningWithAsos' (without quotes) to replace the default name, then press Enter to confirm the new name.
steps.successMessage:
🎉 Perfect! You've successfully created and named your folder!
You now know the basics of file management!

errorMessages.timeout: Type the new name and press Enter to confirm it.
errorMessages.wrongName: Make sure you type 'LearningWithAsos' as the folder name.

hints: The folder name should be highlighted - just start typing
Type: LearningWithAsos
Press Enter when you're done typing
If the name isn't highlighted, try right-clicking the folder and selecting 'Rename'

steps.instruction: Double-click to open your new folder
steps.detailedInstruction: Double-click on the 'LearningWithAsos' folder you just created. This will open the folder and show its contents (which should be empty since it's new).
steps.successMessage: Great! You opened the folder. It's empty because it's brand new.

errorMessages.timeout: Double-click on the LearningWithAsos folder to open it.
errorMessages.wrongFolder: Make sure you're double-clicking on the right folder.

hints: Double-click means click twice quickly
Click on the LearningWithAsos folder
The folder should open and show an empty space inside
The address bar should show the folder name

steps.instruction: Navigate back to Desktop using the back button or address bar
steps.detailedInstruction: Click the back button (←) in your file manager, or click on 'Desktop' in the address bar/breadcrumb navigation to go back to the Desktop folder.
steps.successMessage:
🎉 Excellent! You've mastered basic file navigation!
You can now create folders, rename them, and navigate between them!

errorMessages.timeout: Look for a back button (←) or click 'Desktop' in the address bar.
errorMessages.stillInFolder: Make sure you navigate back to the Desktop folder.

hints: Look for a back arrow button (←) near the top of the window
Or click on 'Desktop' in the address bar
You can also click 'Desktop' in the left sidebar
You should see your LearningWithAsos folder on the Desktop
